Missing at random verification

Source: R/verification.R
mar.Rd

mar() is the assumption that verification depends only on the test results. Once the response profile is known, the disease status does not change the probability of being verified. The function has no arguments.

Usage

mar()

Value

An object of class mar.

Details

Let \(V = 1\) indicate that a subject is verified, \(T\) be the response profile and \(D\) the disease status, and let \(\lambda_{t,d} = P(V = 1 \mid T = t, D = d)\). The assumption is $$\lambda_{t,1} = \lambda_{t,0} = \lambda_t \quad \textrm{for every profile } t,$$ so the probability of verification depends on the profile only.

Equivalently, among subjects with the same profile \(t\), verified and unverified subjects have the same proportion of diseased: $$P(D = 1 \mid T = t, V = 1) = P(D = 1 \mid T = t, V = 0) = P(D = 1 \mid T = t).$$ Verification therefore carries no information on the disease beyond the test results.

Under this assumption the verification process is ignorable and can be left out of the likelihood. Let \(n_{t,d}\) be the number of verified subjects with profile \(t\) and disease status \(d\), \(u_t\) the number of unverified subjects with profile \(t\), \(\pi = P(D = 1)\) the prevalence, \(\pi_1 = \pi\), \(\pi_0 = 1 - \pi\), and \(\theta_{d,t} = P(T = t \mid D = d)\). The log-likelihood of the observed counts is $$\ell = \sum_t \Big[\sum_d n_{t,d} \log(\pi_d\,\theta_{d,t}\,\lambda_{t,d}) + u_t \log \sum_d \pi_d\,\theta_{d,t}\,(1 - \lambda_{t,d})\Big].$$ Setting \(\lambda_{t,d} = \lambda_t\) splits it into two parts, $$\ell = \ell_D + \ell_V,$$ $$\ell_D = \sum_t \Big[\sum_d n_{t,d} \log(\pi_d\,\theta_{d,t}) + u_t \log \sum_d \pi_d\,\theta_{d,t}\Big], \qquad \ell_V = \sum_t \Big[(n_{t,1} + n_{t,0}) \log \lambda_t + u_t \log(1 - \lambda_t)\Big].$$ The verification probabilities \(\lambda_t\) appear only in \(\ell_V\). Inference on the prevalence and on the test distributions is based on \(\ell_D\), and the unverified subjects contribute to it through the totals \(u_t\).

MAR is plausible when the choice of who undergoes the reference standard is made from the test results alone, for example when a protocol prescribes the reference test for every subject with a given test pattern, and no other information related to the disease affects the choice. It is doubtful when the decision to verify uses information on the disease that the tests do not capture, such as symptoms, medical history or clinical suspicion, or when, within the same profile, subjects who are more likely to be diseased are verified more often. In those cases the proportion of diseased among verified subjects differs from that among unverified subjects with the same profile, and the estimates obtained under MAR are biased. The data do not contain information on whether MAR holds, so its plausibility must be judged on substantive grounds. The alternative in which verification also depends on the disease status is missing not at random.

Profiles that are never verified are compatible with MAR, but for them the data give no information on the proportion of diseased: there are no verified subjects from which to estimate it. What is concluded about it comes entirely from an assumption: a prior on that proportion, or a structure imposed on the dependence between the tests.

See also

mnar(), verification_mechanism

Examples

mar()
#> <mar> verification depends only on the test results
